column1: # The verification is a custom TARGET and NOT a custom command with an
# OUTPUT file. A custom command with an OUTPUT file is considered
# up-to-date whenever that file exists and is newer than its
# dependencies, which is exactly the stale-stamp hazard the ACT
# forbids. A custom target's command ALWAYS runs, so the object
# content is checked on every relevant production build.
# THE FAIL-CLOSED VERIFIER, EXERCISED IN FOUR DIRECTIONS
# The verifier ALSO rejects, by construction and as documented in the
# script: an invalid object (REJECT_INVALID_OBJECT), a symbol carried
# only as UNDEFINED (REJECT_UNDEFINED_SYMBOL), a symbol carried only
# as LOCAL (REJECT_LOCAL_SYMBOL), and a DUPLICATE definition
# THE CONFIGURE STEP ALSO FAILS CLOSED
